classes.note: 222 members since 2004 (Art. 46: Johor 26, Kedah 15, Kelantan 14, Melaka 6, Negeri Sembilan 8, Pahang 14, Pulau Pinang 13, Perak 24, Perlis 3, Sabah 25, Sarawak 31, Selangor 22, Terengganu 8, Kuala Lumpur 11, Labuan 1, Putrajaya 1), each elected by plurality in a single-member constituency. classes.name: Pilihan Raya Umum Dewan Undangan Negeri
classes.finest_note: Published per state constituency in the open data (with the general election file for concurrent polls); polling-district and stream counts are not published.
classes.note: Thirteen single-chamber assemblies elected by plurality in single-member state constituencies: Perlis 15, Kedah 36, Kelantan 45, Terengganu 32, Pulau Pinang 40, Perak 59, Pahang 42, Selangor 56, Negeri Sembilan 36, Melaka 28, Johor 56, Sabah 73 (plus nominated members), and Sarawak 82 at its 2021 election. An assembly lasts five years from its first sitting and polls within sixty days of dissolution (Eighth Schedule, Part I, and the state constitutions); most Peninsular states dissolve with Parliament, while Sabah and Sarawak, and since 2021 Melaka, Johor, and six others, poll on their own dates. Sabah's first direct state election was in 1967 and Sarawak's in 1970; Singapore held a state election in September 1963 as a state of Malaysia.
classes.locator: https://lom.agc.gov.my/federal-constitution.php (Art. 113 and Arts. 116-117; Eighth Schedule, Part I)

cadence.locator: https://lom.agc.gov.my/federal-constitution.php (Eighth Schedule, Part I: a State Legislative Assembly continues for five years from its first meeting; a general election within sixty days of dissolution)
cadence.vacancy_rule: A casual vacancy is filled by a by-election within sixty days, except within two years of the assembly's expiry

classes.name: Pilihan Raya Majlis Perundangan Persekutuan
classes.name_en: Federal Legislative Council election (Federation of Malaya)
classes.note: The first federal election in Malaya, held on 27 July 1955, filled the 52 elected seats of the Federal Legislative Council by plurality in single-member constituencies; the Alliance won 51 of the 52 (National Archives of Malaysia). The Council gave way to Parliament under the 1957 Constitution, whose first Dewan Rakyat was elected in 1959. The Election Commission was set up only in 1957 and its list of elections starts in 1959; no official online source publishes the 1955 constituency returns.

dates.quote: Pada hari ini dalam tahun 1955, Pilihan Raya Persekutuan pertama di Persekutuan Tanah Melayu diadakan. [...] Dalam pilihan raya ini, Parti Perikatan memenangi 51 buah kerusi daripada 52 buah yang dipertandingkan.
dates.note: First federal election; 52 elected seats, one per constituency. By-elections to the Council before 1959 are not yet counted from an official source.

classes.name: Pilihan Raya Majlis Negeri dan Majlis Undangan Negeri Selat
classes.name_en: State and Settlement Council elections before independence
classes.note: Elected seats on the State Councils of the Malay states and the Settlement Councils of Penang and Malacca, first filled in 1954-1955 under the Federation of Malaya Agreement 1948; replaced by the State Legislative Assemblies elected in 1959. The Johore State Council first sat with publicly elected members on 23 November 1954, so the first of these elections was held in 1954 (National Archives of Malaysia). No official online source gives the polling days or seat counts.

dates.note: State and Settlement Council elections, the first in Johore in 1954; not yet counted from an official source.
dates.quote: Pada hari ini dalam tahun 1954, Majlis Mesyuarat Negeri Johor telah bermesyuarat buat pertama kalinya semenjak ahli-ahli mesyuaratnya yang baru, dipilih oleh orang ramai.

classes.name: Pemilihan ahli Dewan Rakyat oleh Dewan Undangan Sabah, Sarawak, dan Singapura
classes.name_en: Dewan Rakyat members chosen by the Sabah, Sarawak, and Singapore assemblies
classes.disposition_reason: At Malaysia's formation the members for Sabah, Sarawak, and Singapore were chosen by their state legislatures, not by voters, until each held a direct parliamentary election (Sabah 1969, Sarawak 1970).

classes.name: Pemilihan Senator Dewan Negara oleh Dewan Undangan Negeri
classes.name_en: Senate (Dewan Negara) members elected by the state assemblies
classes.disposition_reason: Each State Legislative Assembly elects two senators by resolution (Art. 45(1)(a)); the other 44 are appointed. The Election Commission runs no poll and no count is published, and the direct election of senators that Art. 45(4) and Art. 120 allow has never been enacted.

classes.name: Pemilihan Yang di-Pertuan Agong oleh Majlis Raja-Raja
classes.name_en: Election of the Supreme Head of the Federation by the Conference of Rulers
classes.disposition_reason: The nine hereditary Rulers elect the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and his deputy for five years by secret ballot in the Conference of Rulers (Art. 32 and Third Schedule); there is no public vote and no published count.

classes.name: Perdana Menteri, Menteri Besar, Ketua Menteri, dan Yang di-Pertua Negeri
classes.disposition_reason: The Prime Minister (Art. 43) and each state's Menteri Besar or Chief Minister are appointed from the assembly majority, the Rulers are hereditary, the governors of Melaka, Pulau Pinang, Sabah, and Sarawak are appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, and Negeri Sembilan's Ruler is chosen by its four Undang; no executive is elected by voters.

classes.name: Pilihan Raya Kerajaan Tempatan
classes.note: Municipal, town, and local council elections began with George Town in December 1951 and Kuala Lumpur in February 1952, spread to Sarawak's district councils and North Borneo's local councils before 1963, and were suspended in March 1965 during the confrontation with Indonesia; the Local Government Act 1976 made all councillors appointed (s. 15 ends local government elections). Penang's 2012 enactment to restore them was held void by the Federal Court in 2014. The class ends in 1976, the year of Act 171; the dates of the first and last polls are not yet read from an official text.
classes.locator: Local Government Act 1976 [Act 171], s. 15 (cesser of local government elections)

dates.note: Local council elections from George Town's first in December 1951 to the suspension of March 1965; not yet counted.

classes.name: Jawatankuasa Pembangunan dan Keselamatan Kampung dan ketua kampung
classes.disposition_reason: Village heads (ketua kampung, penghulu) and village development and security committees are appointed by the state governments; no public election is held.

classes.name: Referendum
classes.disposition_reason: Neither the Federal Constitution nor the Elections Act 1958 provides for a referendum or a recall, and none has been held; constitutional amendments pass by two-thirds of each house of Parliament (Art. 159).

classes.name: Hakim mahkamah atasan dan mahkamah syariah
classes.disposition_reason: Superior court judges are appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the Prime Minister's advice after consulting the Conference of Rulers (Art. 122B), and syariah judges by the state Rulers; none is elected.

classes.name: Pemilihan calon parti
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose candidates under their own constitutions; the Election Commission runs no primary and candidates are nominated directly on nomination day (Elections Act 1958 and its regulations).

classes.name: Pilihan raya persatuan, kesatuan sekerja, koperasi, dan majlis pelajar
classes.name_en: Associations, trade unions, cooperatives, and student councils
classes.disposition_reason: Held by each body under its own rules (the Commission only lends equipment and training for some school and university polls); they elect no public office.
